rationale: Standard instruction lines from the SAT. These are exempt from the originality check and may be used verbatim in original items. Two independent reasons. (1) They are short functional phrases dictated by their purpose - the US Copyright Office does not register 'words and short phrases' (37 CFR 202.1(a)), and merger applies where an idea has only a few natural expressions. (2) Reuse establishes it as boilerplate rather than authorship: each line below appears on at least 10 different items, and the most common appears on 420. This exemption covers instruction lines ONLY. Passages, answer choices and rationales are where the expression lives, and the originality check stays strict on all of them.
